newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end mostly higher, platinum up.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end mostly higher, platinum up.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo gold futures closed mostly higher on Monday, reflecting spot gold's rise during Asian trading hours, traders said.
Benchmark June gold futures ended up two yen at 1,164 yen.
Spot gold was quoted at $321.70/322.20 per ounce at 0733 GMT, against $321.00/60 in New York on Friday.

"Local investors were seen buying light volumes. But the buying orders failed to continue throughout the day," a brokerage house trader said. "Last week, falling bullion prices aggravated the bearish mood, but at the moment I do not expect prices to fall further."
Tokyo platinum futures ended higher on Monday as physical supplies remained tight, traders said.
Prices ranged from three to 30 yen higher, with benchmark June 1998 ending up eight yen at 1,313 yen per gram.
Russia has resumed its PGMs exports for this year, but persistant concerns over the stability of Russian supplies next year are seen as a bullish factor for the market.
"The Russian factor will be a wild card for a while," a platinum trader at a major trade house said.
Palladium futures ranged from 11 yen lower to 10 yen higher, with benchmark June down 11 yen at 513 yen per gram.
Benchmark June silver was unchanged from Friday's close at 162.2 yen per 10 grams.
